about: Learner cards use a_note, b_note, and labeled examples only. verified true means support holds a sense excerpt from a page that was opened. verified false means the URL only names a headword page and the sense was not re-checked in this pass. fr_neuf_num is not compared with nouveau. poêle is not compared with fourneau.

edges.a_note: Année is a year as a stretch of time, or one particular year. An is the year you count, as in ages.
edges.b_note: An is the year you count, as in ages. Année is a year as a stretch of time.
b_ex: Cette année, je vis à Lyon.
This year I live in Lyon.

edges.a_note: Journée is the day as a stretch of time. Jour is a day you count, or daylight.
edges.b_note: Jour is a day you count, or daylight. Journée is the whole length of the day.
a_ex: Il y a sept jours dans une semaine.
There are seven days in a week.

edges.a_note: Matinée is the morning as a stretch of time. Matin is the morning as a time of day.
edges.b_note: Matin is the morning as a point in the day (ce matin). Matinée is the whole morning.

edges.a_note: Soirée is the evening as a stretch of time, and it can be an evening party. Soir is the evening as a time of day.
edges.b_note: Soir is the evening as a time of day. Soirée is the whole evening, or a party.
b_ex: Nous avons passé la soirée ensemble.

edges.a_note: Connaître is to be familiar with a person, a place, or a thing. Savoir is to know a fact, or how to do something.
edges.b_note: Savoir is to know a fact or how to do something. Connaître is to be familiar with someone or something.

edges.a_note: Quitter names the person or place you leave. Partir does not take that direct object. For the place, partir takes de.
edges.b_note: Partir has no direct object (partir de Paris). Quitter takes the person or place directly.

edges.a_note: Laisser is to leave something behind, or to let someone do something. Partir is to leave, yourself.
edges.b_note: Partir is to go away. Laisser is to leave something or someone behind, or to allow it.
b_ex: J'ai laissé mes clés à la maison.
I left my keys at home.

edges.a_note: Laisser is to leave something behind or to let someone act. Quitter is to leave a person or a place.
edges.b_note: Quitter is to leave a person or a place. Laisser is to leave something behind, or to let.

edges.a_note: Sortir is to go out, or to come out of a place. Partir is to leave, to set off.
edges.b_note: Partir is to set off. Sortir is to go out or to exit.
a_ex: Le train part à neuf heures.

edges.a_note: Amener is usual for a person or an animal. Apporter is usual for a thing you carry.
edges.b_note: Apporter is usual for a thing. Amener is usual for a person or an animal.

edges.a_note: Emmener is to take a person or an animal along. Emporter is to take a thing away.
edges.b_note: Emporter is to take a thing away. Emmener is to take a person or an animal along.
b_ex: Elle emmène les enfants au parc.
She is taking the children to the park.

edges.a_note: Emporter is to take a thing away. Apporter is to bring a thing here.
edges.b_note: Apporter is to bring a thing here. Emporter is to take a thing away.

edges.a_note: Emmener is to take a person away from here. Amener is to bring a person here.
edges.b_note: Amener is to bring a person here. Emmener is to take a person away.

edges.a_note: Vivre is to be alive, or to live your life. It can also say where you live. Habiter is specifically to reside in a place.
edges.b_note: Habiter is to live in a place. Vivre can mean that too, and it also means to be alive.

edges.a_note: Docteur is what you usually call the person, and it can mean someone with a doctorate. Médecin is the profession.
edges.b_note: Médecin is the job. Docteur is the title you use when you speak to one.

edges.a_note: Peuple is a people, a nation, or ordinary people as a group. Gens is people in general.
edges.b_note: Gens is people in general. Peuple is a nation, or the common people.
a_ex: Il y a beaucoup de gens.
There are a lot of people.

edges.a_note: Nombre is a quantity, or a number you do math with. Numéro is a number that labels something, like a phone or a house.
edges.b_note: Numéro is a label in a series. Nombre is how many, or a number in math.
b_ex: Choisis un nombre entre un et dix.
Pick a number between one and ten.

edges.a_note: Chiffre is a digit, from 0 to 9, or a figure people quote. Nombre is the whole number or the quantity.
edges.b_note: Nombre is a quantity or a full number. Chiffre is one digit, or a quoted figure.

edges.a_note: Chiffre is a single digit. Numéro is the number given to a phone, a seat, or a house.
edges.b_note: Numéro labels one thing in a series. Chiffre is a digit, or a figure.

edges.a_note: Fleuve is a large river, and it usually reaches the sea. Rivière is a smaller river. It may join a fleuve, a lake, or the sea.
edges.b_note: Rivière is a smaller river, which may join a fleuve, a lake, or the sea. Fleuve is a large river, usually one that reaches the sea.

edges.a_note: Gratuit means free of charge. Libre means available, or free to act.
edges.b_note: Libre means available or free to do something. Gratuit means you do not pay.

edges.a_note: Incendie is a damaging fire, a blaze in a building or a forest. Feu is fire in general, a flame, or a traffic light.
edges.b_note: Feu is fire, a flame, or a traffic light. Incendie is a fire that burns a place.

edges.a_note: Envers is toward a person, about feelings or behavior. Vers is toward a place, or around a time.
edges.b_note: Vers is toward a place or about a time. Envers is how you act toward someone.

edges.a_note: Étudiant is a college or university student. Élève is a pupil in school.
edges.b_note: Élève is a school pupil. Étudiant is a student in higher education.

edges.a_note: Écolier is a grade-school pupil. Élève is any pupil.
edges.b_note: Élève is the general word for a pupil. Écolier is a child in grade school.

edges.a_note: Lycéen is a high-school student. Étudiant is usually college or university.
edges.b_note: Étudiant is usually higher education. Lycéen is a student at a lycée.

edges.a_note: Figure is also a person's face, a bit more familiar, and it can be a drawn shape. Visage is the usual word for a face.
edges.b_note: Visage is the usual word for a person's face. Figure is a face too, or a shape in a drawing.

edges.a_note: Face is a side or a surface. For a person's face, visage is the usual word. Face shows up in phrases like face à.
edges.b_note: Visage is a person's face. Face is a side or a surface, as in face à.

edges.a_note: Face is a side or a surface. Figure is a person's face, or a drawn shape.
edges.b_note: Figure is a face or a drawn shape. Face is a side or a surface.

edges.a_note: Mémoire is your ability to remember, or a written account. Souvenir is one memory of something that happened, or a keepsake.
edges.b_note: Souvenir is a particular memory, or a keepsake. Mémoire is the faculty of memory.

edges.a_note: Square is a small public garden. Place is a town square, a seat, or an amount of room.
edges.b_note: Place is a town square, a seat, or space. Square is a small planted garden in a city.

edges.a_note: Queue is the usual word for people waiting (faire la queue), and it is also a tail. File is that waiting line too.
edges.b_note: File is a waiting line (une file d'attente). Queue is the same idea, and it is also an animal's tail.

edges.a_note: File is a line of people or cars waiting. Ligne is a line you draw, a row, or a bus or train line.
edges.b_note: Ligne is a drawn line or a transit line, not the queue. File is people or cars waiting.

edges.a_note: Queue is the line you wait in, or a tail. Ligne is a line you draw, or a bus or train line.
edges.b_note: Ligne is not the waiting line. Queue is the line you wait in, or a tail.

edges.a_note: Commande is an order you place for food or goods. Ordre is a command, or the way things are arranged.
edges.b_note: Ordre is a command or an arrangement. Commande is an order for goods or a meal.

edges.a_note: Ordonner is to order someone to do something, or to arrange. Commander is to order goods, or to be in command.
edges.b_note: Commander is to order goods, or to command. Ordonner is to order someone to act, or to put things in order.

edges.a_note: Suivant is often the next one in a series. Prochain is often the next one coming up in time.
edges.b_note: Prochain is often the next one in time. Suivant is often the following item in a list.

edges.a_note: Before the noun, ancien often means former. After the noun, it can mean ancient or long-standing. Vieux is old in age, or worn out.
edges.b_note: Vieux is old or worn. Ancien often means former before the noun, and ancient or long-standing after it.

edges.a_note: Pareil means alike, the same kind. Même points to the same one.
edges.b_note: Même is the very same one. Pareil is similar or alike.

edges.a_note: Lorsque is close to quand in a statement, and a little more formal. Lorsque does not ask a question.
edges.b_note: Quand can ask a question. Lorsque cannot. In a statement they are close, and lorsque is a little more formal.

edges.a_note: Si means yes when you contradict a negative question or statement. Oui is yes to a positive one. Si also means if.
edges.b_note: Oui answers a positive question. Si answers a negative one, and it also means if.
b_ex: You're not coming? — Yes, I am!

edges.a_note: S'il vous plaît is please for vous: polite, or more than one person. S'il te plaît is for one person you know well.
edges.b_note: S'il te plaît is please for tu. S'il vous plaît is the polite or plural please.

edges.a_note: Vous is for more than one person, or for one person you speak to politely. Tu is for one person you know well, a child, or family.
edges.b_note: Tu is one person, familiar. Vous is polite for one person, or any group.

edges.a_note: Toi is the stressed form, as in c'est toi. Tu is the subject in an ordinary sentence.
edges.b_note: Tu is the ordinary subject. Toi is stressed, for emphasis or after a preposition.

edges.a_note: Toi is the stressed form. Te is the unstressed object before the verb.
edges.b_note: Te comes before the verb. Toi is stressed, or used after a preposition.

edges.a_note: Votre is your for vous: polite or plural. Ton is your for tu, one person you know well.
edges.b_note: Ton goes with tu. Votre goes with vous.

edges.a_note: Aux is à + les, for a plural. Au is à + le, for one masculine noun.
edges.b_note: Au is à + le. Aux is à + les.

edges.a_note: Nous is we or us, and it is the form you often see in writing. On is the everyday word for we, and it also means people in general.
edges.b_note: On often means we in conversation, and it can mean people in general. Nous is we or us.

edges.a_note: Davantage means more, and the TLFi presents it as modifying a verb. It is not the word in front of an adjective: that is plus (plus grand). Ne...plus, not davantage, is the ordinary way to say no longer.
edges.b_note: Plus is the usual word for more, including before an adjective, and with ne it means no longer. Davantage means more when it modifies a verb, not no longer.

support.excerpt: Davantage modifie un verbe et la comparaison est implicite.

edges.a_note: Fric is informal for money. Argent is the ordinary word, and it also means silver.
edges.b_note: Argent is the ordinary word for money. Fric is casual slang.

edges.a_note: Nana is an informal word for a girl or a young woman. Fille is girl, and it also means daughter.
edges.b_note: Fille is the ordinary word. Nana is informal.

edges.a_note: Emploi is a job, a position, and it can mean a use. Travail is work in general, or a task.
edges.b_note: Travail is work or a task. Emploi is employment, a position, or a use.

edges.a_note: Boulot is an informal word for work or a job. Travail is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Travail is the ordinary word. Boulot is informal.

edges.a_note: Boulot is informal for a job or for work. Emploi is a position, more neutral, and it can mean a use.
edges.b_note: Emploi is a job or a use. Boulot is the informal word.

edges.a_note: When poste is masculine, it can be a job or a post, and it is also a TV or radio set. Emploi is a job or a use.
edges.b_note: Emploi is a job or a use. The masculine poste can be that job, or a TV or radio set.

edges.a_note: Ouvrage is a work you produce, such as a book, and it is a bit more formal. Travail is work in general.
edges.b_note: Travail is work in general. Ouvrage is a particular work, often a book.

edges.a_note: Œuvre is a work of art, or someone's life's work. Travail is work in general.
edges.b_note: Travail is work or a task. Œuvre is a work of art or a body of work.

edges.a_note: Boutique is often a smaller shop. Magasin is a shop, and it can be a larger store.
edges.b_note: Magasin can be a larger store. Boutique is often a smaller shop.

edges.a_note: Foncé is dark as a color (bleu foncé). Sombre is dark as in dim light, or somber.
edges.b_note: Sombre is poorly lit, or somber. Foncé is a dark shade of a color.

edges.a_note: Demi can stand in front of a noun (une demi-heure) or after it with et (deux heures et demie; the feminine is demie). Moitié is a half of something (la moitié).
edges.b_note: Moitié is half of a whole. Demi is also the half you add with et, and it agrees: une heure et demie, deux ans et demi.

support.excerpt: Il a deux ans et demi; il est une heure et demie.

b_ex: Il est deux heures et demie.

edges.a_note: Ticket is often a small slip: a metro ride, a receipt, a cloakroom slip. Billet is often a train or plane ticket, or a banknote.
edges.b_note: Billet is often a travel ticket or a banknote. Ticket is often the smaller slip.

edges.a_note: Pendule is a clock you put on a wall or a shelf. Horloge is a large clock, often on a tower.
edges.b_note: Horloge is a large clock. Pendule is a household clock.

edges.a_note: Montre is a watch you wear. Horloge is a large clock.
edges.b_note: Horloge is a large clock. Montre is a wristwatch or a pocket watch.

edges.a_note: Montre is a watch you wear. Pendule is a clock in a room.
edges.b_note: Pendule is a wall or shelf clock. Montre is a watch.

edges.a_note: Cuisiner is to cook a meal, the activity. Cuire is to cook with heat, and food itself can cuire.
edges.b_note: Cuire is cooking by heat. Cuisiner is preparing a meal.

edges.a_note: Carnet is a small notebook, or a booklet of tickets or forms. Cahier is a school exercise book.
edges.b_note: Cahier is a school notebook. Carnet is a small notebook or a booklet.

edges.a_note: Soulier is a low shoe. Usito marks that use as characteristic of Quebec and Canadian French, where it is an ordinary word, not a formal one. In France, chaussure is the usual word.
edges.b_note: Chaussure is the usual word in France. Soulier is ordinary in Quebec and Canadian French for the same kind of shoe.

support.excerpt: Chaussure à tige basse et à semelle rigide qui couvre le pied. Cet emploi est caractéristique de la variété de français qui a cours au Québec.

edges.a_note: Cesser is to stop or to come to an end, often a bit more formal. Arrêter is to stop something or someone, and it can mean to arrest.
edges.b_note: Arrêter is the everyday verb for making something stop. Cesser is to cease, often on its own.

edges.a_note: Stopper is an informal word for to stop. Arrêter is the ordinary verb, and it can mean to arrest.
edges.b_note: Arrêter is the ordinary verb. Stopper is informal.

edges.a_note: Se promener is to go for a walk. Promener is also to walk a dog. Marcher is to walk.
edges.b_note: Marcher is to walk. Promener is to take someone or a dog for a walk.

edges.a_note: Bosser is informal for to work. Travailler is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Travailler is the ordinary word. Bosser is informal.

edges.a_note: Bouquiner is informal for to read, often for pleasure. Lire is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Lire is the ordinary word. Bouquiner is informal.

edges.a_note: Bouquin is an informal word for a book. Livre is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Livre is the ordinary word. Bouquin is informal.

edges.a_note: Bagnole is informal for a car, sometimes an old one. Voiture is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Voiture is the ordinary word. Bagnole is informal.

edges.a_note: Rigoler is informal for to laugh. Rire is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Rire is the ordinary word. Rigoler is informal.

edges.a_note: Complet means complete, or full with no room left. Plein means full of something.
edges.b_note: Plein is full of something. Complet is complete, or fully booked.

edges.a_note: Lancer is to throw in a direction, or to launch. Jeter is to throw, and often to throw away.
edges.b_note: Jeter is to throw, often away. Lancer is to throw toward something, or to launch.

edges.a_note: Briser is to break violently or to shatter. Casser is the everyday word for to break.
edges.b_note: Casser is the everyday word. Briser is harsher: to shatter.

edges.a_note: Rompre is to break off, as a relationship or a bond, and it is more formal. Casser is the everyday word for to break.
edges.b_note: Casser is the everyday word for to break. Rompre is often to break off a bond.

edges.a_note: Rompre is often to break off a bond or an agreement. Briser is to shatter something.
edges.b_note: Briser is to shatter. Rompre is to break off.

edges.a_note: Clore is formal, often to close a period, a list, or a discussion. Fermer is the everyday word, as in closing a door.
edges.b_note: Fermer is the everyday word. Clore is formal.

edges.a_note: Paroi is a side, a partition, or the inner surface of something. Mur is a wall of a building.
edges.b_note: Mur is a building wall. Paroi is a side or an inner surface.

edges.a_note: Muraille is a high defensive wall, as around a city. Mur is an ordinary wall.
edges.b_note: Mur is an ordinary wall. Muraille is a rampart.

edges.a_note: Poil is a body hair or an animal's hair. Cheveu is a hair on the head.
edges.b_note: Cheveu is a hair of the head. Poil is body hair or animal hair.

edges.a_note: Apparaître is to come into sight. Paraître is to seem, or to be published.
edges.b_note: Paraître is to seem, or to appear in print. Apparaître is to come into view.

edges.a_note: Figurer is to appear on a list or in a group, or to imagine. Paraître is to seem, or to be published.
edges.b_note: Paraître is to seem. Figurer is to be included in a list, or to picture something.

edges.a_note: Figurer is to be listed or to imagine, not to come into sight. Apparaître is to come into view.
edges.b_note: Apparaître is to come into view. Figurer is to appear on a list, or to imagine.

edges.a_note: Rater is to miss or to fail, and it is a bit informal. Manquer is to miss a train or a person, or to lack.
edges.b_note: Manquer is to miss something, or not to have enough. Rater is informal for to fail or to miss.

edges.a_note: Siéger is to sit in an official seat, as on a council, or for an office to have its headquarters somewhere. S'asseoir is to sit down.
edges.b_note: S'asseoir is to sit down. Siéger is to hold a session, or for a company to have its seat in a city.

support.excerpt: Être assis à une place officielle. Avoir son siège officiellement établi (à).

edges.a_note: Ballon is a large ball you inflate, or a balloon. Balle is a small ball, and it can be a bullet.
edges.b_note: Balle is a small ball or a bullet. Ballon is an inflatable ball or a balloon.

edges.a_note: Boule is a bowl, like a pétanque ball, or a round lump. Balle is a small ball for a game, or a bullet.
edges.b_note: Balle is a small game ball or a bullet. Boule is a heavy bowl or a round lump.

edges.a_note: Boule is a heavy bowl or a round lump. Ballon is an inflatable ball or a balloon.
edges.b_note: Ballon is inflatable. Boule is a solid bowl.

edges.a_note: Pelote is a ball of yarn, or the ball in pelota. Balle is a small game ball, or a bullet.
edges.b_note: Balle is a small ball or a bullet. Pelote is yarn wound into a ball, or a pelota ball.

edges.a_note: Marrant is informal for funny. Drôle is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Drôle is the ordinary word. Marrant is informal.

edges.a_note: Rigolo is informal for funny. Drôle is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Drôle is the ordinary word. Rigolo is informal.

edges.a_note: Sérieux is serious as a person, or not a joke. Grave is serious as in severe. The two overlap for problems.
edges.b_note: Grave is severe. Sérieux is serious-minded, or genuinely meant. A problem can be either.

edges.a_note: Tarif is a rate or a price list. Prix is the price of one thing, and it is also a prize.
edges.b_note: Prix is what you pay, or a prize. Tarif is a scale of prices.

edges.a_note: Déplacer is to move something from one place to another. Bouger is to move or to budge.
edges.b_note: Bouger is to move yourself or to budge. Déplacer is to shift something else.

edges.a_note: Émouvoir is to move someone emotionally. Bouger is to move physically.
edges.b_note: Bouger is physical movement. Émouvoir is to move someone inside.

edges.a_note: Mouvoir is a formal verb for to move. Bouger is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Bouger is ordinary. Mouvoir is formal.

edges.a_note: Charrier is to cart something along, and in speech it can mean to tease. Porter is to carry, or to wear.
edges.b_note: Porter is to carry or to wear. Charrier is to haul, or to kid someone.

edges.a_note: Mettre is to put something on, or to put it somewhere. Porter is to wear it, or to carry it.
edges.b_note: Porter is to wear or to carry. Mettre is to put on, or to put in a place.

edges.a_note: Rechercher is a more deliberate or formal search, as when the police look for someone. Chercher is the everyday word.
edges.b_note: Chercher is the everyday word for to look for. Rechercher is a more formal or sustained search.

edges.a_note: Tenter is to try, a bit more formal, and it also means to tempt. Essayer is the everyday word for to try.
edges.b_note: Essayer is to try, or to try on. Tenter is to attempt, or to tempt someone.

edges.a_note: Tâcher de is to make an effort to do something. Essayer is the everyday word for to try.
edges.b_note: Essayer is the everyday word. Tâcher de is to try to, with an effort.

edges.a_note: Conserver is to keep something in good condition, or to preserve it. Garder is to keep, to hold on to, or to look after.
edges.b_note: Garder is to keep or to look after. Conserver is to preserve.

edges.a_note: Remporter is to win a match, a prize, or a victory. Gagner is to win, and also to earn money.
edges.b_note: Gagner is to win or to earn. Remporter is to carry off a victory or a prize.

edges.a_note: Gosse is informal for a kid. Enfant is the ordinary word for a child.
edges.b_note: Enfant is the ordinary word. Gosse is informal.

edges.a_note: Gamin is informal for a kid. Enfant is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Enfant is the ordinary word. Gamin is informal.

edges.a_note: Môme is informal for a kid. Enfant is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Enfant is the ordinary word. Môme is informal.

edges.a_note: Achever is to complete the last part of something. Finir is the everyday word for to finish. Finir and terminer are close for an ordinary task.
edges.b_note: Finir is the everyday word for to finish. Achever stresses the last step.

edges.a_note: Achever stresses the last step of a task. Terminer is to finish a task. For an ordinary task, terminer and finir are close.
edges.b_note: Terminer is to finish a task. Achever is to bring it to the last step.

edges.a_note: Décès is the official or administrative word. Mort is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Mort is the ordinary word. Décès is the word on forms and in the news.

edges.a_note: Crainte is more formal, often a worry about what might happen. Peur is fear, including a sudden fright.
edges.b_note: Peur is fear. Crainte is a more formal worry that something may happen.

edges.a_note: Prof is the informal short form. Professeur is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Professeur is the ordinary word. Prof is informal.

edges.a_note: Enseignant is a teacher in general. Professeur covers secondary and university teachers, and primary teachers are professeurs des écoles, so the title is not limited to older students.
edges.b_note: Professeur is a teaching title, including professeur des écoles in primary school. Enseignant is the general word for a teacher.

support.excerpt: professeur de collège, de lycée, d'université, de faculté.

edges.a_note: Vécu is what you have lived through. Expérience is experience, and it is also an experiment.
edges.b_note: Expérience is experience or an experiment. Vécu is lived experience.

edges.a_note: Caractère is personality, or a printed character. Personnage is a character in a story, or an important person.
edges.b_note: Personnage is a character in a story. Caractère is personality, or a letter of type.

edges.a_note: Prévenir is usually to warn or to notify. It can mean to prevent, but empêcher is the usual verb for stopping something from happening.
edges.b_note: Empêcher is to prevent, or to keep someone from doing something. Prévenir is usually to let someone know ahead of time.

edges.a_note: Rivage is a shore, often of the sea. Rive is the bank of a river or a lake.
edges.b_note: Rive is a riverbank or a lakeshore. Rivage is more often the seashore.

edges.a_note: Berge is the raised edge of a river, the embankment. Rive is the bank more generally.
edges.b_note: Rive is the bank in general. Berge is the raised edge.

edges.a_note: Archet is the bow of a string instrument. Arc is a bow you shoot with, or an arc.
edges.b_note: Arc is a weapon bow, or a curve. Archet is a violin bow.

edges.a_note: Tuyau is a pipe or hose that carries something, and informally a tip. Pipe is the kind with a bowl and a stem.
edges.b_note: Pipe is the kind with a bowl and a stem. Tuyau carries water or gas, or it is a tip.

edges.a_note: Rentrer is to go back in, or to come home. Revenir is to come back to where the speaker is, or back to a place.
edges.b_note: Revenir is to come back. Rentrer is often to go home, or to go back inside.

edges.a_note: Retourner is to go back, and it also means to turn something over. The person is not necessarily coming to you. Revenir is to come back.
edges.b_note: Revenir is to come back here. Retourner is to go back there, or to flip something over.

edges.a_note: Retourner is to go back to a place, or to turn something over. Rentrer is to go back in or to come home.
edges.b_note: Rentrer is to go home or back inside. Retourner is to go back, or to turn over.

edges.a_note: Langage is the way someone uses words, or a system such as a programming language. Langue is a language such as French, and it is also the tongue.
edges.b_note: Langue is a particular language, or the tongue. Langage is wording, or a system of expression.

edges.a_note: Océan is an ocean, one of the great bodies of water. Mer is a sea, and it is the usual word at the beach.
edges.b_note: Mer is a sea. Océan is an ocean.

edges.a_note: Forêt is a forest. Bois is wood the material, or a smaller woods.
edges.b_note: Bois can be a small woods, or the material wood. Forêt is a forest.

edges.a_note: Temps is time in general, or the weather. Heure is an hour, or the time of day on a clock.
edges.b_note: Heure is the hour or the time by the clock. Temps is time as a stretch, or the weather.

edges.a_note: Bien is the adverb, well, and a noun for what is good. Bon is the adjective, good.
edges.b_note: Bon describes a noun. Bien tells how something is done, or says things are fine.

edges.a_note: Mal is the adverb, badly, and it is an ache in avoir mal. Mauvais is the adjective, bad.
edges.b_note: Mauvais describes a noun. Mal is how something is done, or a pain.

edges.a_note: Salle is a room with a purpose, or a hall. Pièce is a room in a home, and it is also a coin or a play.
edges.b_note: Pièce is one room of a house, a coin, or a play. Salle is a room used for an activity, or a larger hall.

edges.a_note: Durant is a little more formal and often covers a whole period. Pendant is the usual word for during, and with a length it means for.
edges.b_note: Pendant is the ordinary word. With a length of time it means for. Durant is during or throughout, a bit more formal.

edges.a_note: Finalement is in the end, when you look at how things turned out. Enfin is finally, or a spoken well.
edges.b_note: Enfin is finally, or well in speech. Finalement is when the outcome is what you settle on.

edges.a_note: Faute can be a mistake or someone's fault. Erreur is an error or a mistake, not blame.
edges.b_note: Erreur is a mistake. Faute is a fault or a mistake, and c'est ma faute means it's my fault.

edges.a_note: Méprise is a mix-up, misunderstanding what someone meant. Faute is a fault or a mistake.
edges.b_note: Faute is a fault or a mistake. Méprise is taking one thing for another.

edges.a_note: Sentier is a narrow path, often a trail. Chemin is a path or a way, and it can be wider.
edges.b_note: Chemin is a path or a way. Sentier is a narrower trail.

edges.a_note: Route is a road, often between towns or a main road. Rue is a street in a town.
edges.b_note: Rue is a town street. Route is a road for traffic.

edges.a_note: Chemin is a path or a smaller way. Route is a road for cars.
edges.b_note: Route is a road. Chemin is a path or a way.

edges.a_note: Chemin is a path, not usually a town street. Rue is a street with buildings.
edges.b_note: Rue is a street in town. Chemin is a path or a way.

edges.a_note: Bouffer is very informal for to eat. Manger is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Manger is the ordinary word. Bouffer is very informal.

edges.a_note: Entreprise is a business or a firm. Compagnie can be a company too, and it is also the people with you.
edges.b_note: Compagnie is companionship, or a company. Entreprise is a business.

edges.a_note: Lieu is a bit more formal for a place, and it appears in phrases such as au lieu de. Endroit is the everyday word for a spot.
edges.b_note: Endroit is the everyday word for a place. Lieu is more formal, or part of a set phrase.

edges.a_note: Aisé is more formal for easy, and it can mean well-off. Facile is the ordinary word for easy.
edges.b_note: Facile is the ordinary word for easy. Aisé is more formal, or it means comfortably off.

edges.a_note: Haïr is stronger: to hate. Détester is to dislike strongly, the everyday word.
edges.b_note: Détester is the everyday word for to really dislike. Haïr is to hate.

edges.a_note: Vociférer is to shout in anger, and it is stronger and more formal. Crier is to shout or to scream.
edges.b_note: Crier is to shout. Vociférer is to yell furiously.

edges.a_note: Chant is singing, or a chant. Chanson is a song, usually with words.
edges.b_note: Chanson is a song. Chant is the act of singing, or a chant.

edges.a_note: Roux is reddish-brown, especially hair. Rouge is red.
edges.b_note: Rouge is red. Roux is auburn or ginger, not pure red.

edges.a_note: Net is clean in the sense of clear or sharp, or a net amount. Propre is clean, or one's own.
edges.b_note: Propre is clean, or own. Net is clear, sharp, or net of deductions.

edges.a_note: Adorer is stronger than aimer, or it means to worship. Aimer is to like or to love.
edges.b_note: Aimer is to like or to love. Adorer is to love something dearly, or to worship.

edges.a_note: Songer is more literary: to have something in mind. Penser is the ordinary word for to think.
edges.b_note: Penser is the ordinary word. Songer is to be thinking of something, in a more literary tone.

edges.a_note: Séjourner is to stay somewhere for a while, as on a trip. Rester is to stay.
edges.b_note: Rester is to stay. Séjourner is to stay for a period, often away from home.

edges.a_note: Actuellement means currently, these days. It does not mean actually. Maintenant is now.
edges.b_note: Maintenant is now, at this moment. Actuellement is currently, and it is not the word for actually.

edges.a_note: Là can mean there, and in ordinary speech it also means here, where the speaker is (je suis là). Ici is specifically here.
edges.b_note: Ici is here, near the speaker. Là is not only 'there': the TLFi says it can mark the speaker's own place.

support.excerpt: Adverbe de lieu marquant le lieu où se trouve le locuteur ou un lieu plus ou moins éloigné de lui. Monsieur, je suis là depuis une heure.

edges.a_note: Là-bas is over there, a long way off. Ici is here.
edges.b_note: Ici is here, near the speaker. Là-bas is over there.

edges.a_note: Là-bas is a long way off. Là is there, often less distant.
edges.b_note: Là can be there, closer than là-bas. Là-bas is over there.

edges.a_note: Truc is informal for a thing, and it can be a trick. Chose is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Chose is the ordinary word. Truc is informal, or a trick.

edges.a_note: Chuter is to fall, often a sharp drop, and it is used for prices or scores. Tomber is the everyday word.
edges.b_note: Tomber is the everyday word for to fall. Chuter is a drop, often of a number.

edges.a_note: S'évader is to escape from a place that holds you, such as a prison. Échapper is to escape or to avoid, more broadly.
edges.b_note: Échapper is to get away or to avoid. S'évader is to break out of confinement.

edges.a_note: Songe is a literary word for a dream. Rêve is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Rêve is the ordinary word. Songe is literary.

edges.a_note: Épouser takes the person you marry as a direct object. Se marier is to get married.
edges.b_note: Se marier is to get married. Épouser is to marry someone.
a_ex: They are getting married in June.

edges.a_note: Tapage is a loud disturbance. Bruit is noise in general.
edges.b_note: Bruit is noise. Tapage is an uproar.

edges.a_note: Planquer is informal for to hide. Cacher is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Cacher is the ordinary word. Planquer is informal.

edges.a_note: Dada can be a child's word for a horse, or a hobby. Cheval is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Cheval is a horse. Dada is a hobby-horse word, or a pet subject.

edges.a_note: Sursauter is to jump because something startles you. Sauter is to jump.
edges.b_note: Sauter is to jump. Sursauter is to start, to jump at a shock.

edges.a_note: Aborder is to approach a person or a subject, or to reach shore. Approcher is to come nearer.
edges.b_note: Approcher is to come near. Aborder is to go up to someone, to take up a topic, or to land.

edges.a_note: Puissance is power as strength, or a powerful state. Pouvoir is the power to do something, or political power.
edges.b_note: Pouvoir is power you can use, or authority. Puissance is might, or a power in the world.

edges.a_note: Case is a cell in a grid, a pigeonhole, or a box on a form. Boîte is a box or a can.
edges.b_note: Boîte is a box or a can. Case is one square or compartment.

edges.a_note: Recouvrir is to cover something over. Couvrir is to cover, with many extended uses.
edges.b_note: Couvrir is to cover. Recouvrir is to cover over, often completely.

edges.a_note: Pochette is a small pouch, a clutch, or a sleeve. Poche is a pocket.
edges.b_note: Poche is a pocket. Pochette is a little case or a sleeve.

edges.a_note: Parvenir is to manage to reach a place or a result. Atteindre is to reach a place, a level, or a person.
edges.b_note: Atteindre is to reach. Parvenir is to succeed in getting there.

edges.a_note: Animal is the neutral word. Bête is an animal, often a familiar word, and as an adjective it means stupid.
edges.b_note: Bête is a familiar word for an animal. Animal is the ordinary noun.

edges.a_note: Régaler is to treat someone to a good meal. Traiter is to treat, to deal with, or to handle.
edges.b_note: Traiter has many senses: deal with, treat, handle. Régaler is to stand someone a meal.

edges.a_note: Étonner is to astonish, to seem unexpected. Surprendre is to surprise someone, or to catch them at it.
edges.b_note: Surprendre is to surprise or to catch. Étonner is to amaze.

edges.a_note: Clef and clé are the same word for a key. In music, both clé de sol and clef de sol are used for the sign on the staff. Clef is the older spelling.
edges.b_note: Clé is the usual spelling of a key, and clé de sol is standard. Clef is the older spelling of the same word, including the musical sign.

support.excerpt: CLEF, CLÉ. MUSIQUE. Signe placé en tête de la portée. Chacun des trois signes pouvant se placer au commencement de la portée pour indiquer fa, sol ou ut.

edges.a_note: Admettre is to admit that something is true, or to let someone in. Avouer is to confess.
edges.b_note: Avouer is to confess. Admettre is to grant that something is so, or to allow someone in.

edges.a_note: S'enfuir is to run away. Fuir is to flee a place or to avoid something.
edges.b_note: Fuir is to flee or to shun. S'enfuir is to take flight.

edges.a_note: Ressentir is to feel an emotion or a sensation. Éprouver is to feel something strongly, or to put something to the test.
edges.b_note: Éprouver is to feel deeply, or to test. Ressentir is to feel within yourself.

edges.a_note: Ras is cut very short, close to the skin. Court is short in length.
edges.b_note: Court is short. Ras is close-cropped.

edges.a_note: Criminalité is how much crime there is. Crime is one crime, and in French law it is a serious offense.
edges.b_note: Crime is an offense. Criminalité is the amount of crime.

edges.a_note: Pile can be a heap, and it is also a battery. Tas is a heap or a pile of things.
edges.b_note: Tas is a heap. Pile is that kind of heap, or a battery.

edges.a_note: Crever is to burst, and informally it is a rough word for to die. Éclater is to burst or to break out.
edges.b_note: Éclater is to burst. Crever is to burst, or, informally, to die.

edges.a_note: Emplir is a more literary word for to fill. Remplir is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Remplir is ordinary. Emplir is literary.

edges.a_note: Peinture is paint, the art of painting, or a painting. Tableau is one painting, or a board.
edges.b_note: Tableau is a painting or a board. Peinture is paint, or painting as an art.

edges.a_note: Star is a famous performer, from English. Étoile is a star in the sky.
edges.b_note: Étoile is a star in the sky. Star is a celebrity.

edges.a_note: Vedette is a star of the stage or screen. Étoile is a star in the sky.
edges.b_note: Étoile is up in the sky. Vedette is a performer who is a star.

edges.a_note: Vedette is the French word for a star performer. Star is the English loan.
edges.b_note: Star is the loanword. Vedette is the French word.

edges.a_note: Agiter is to wave, to stir, or to disturb. Secouer is to shake something.
edges.b_note: Secouer is to shake. Agiter is to wave or to stir up.

edges.a_note: Colis is a parcel sent by mail or freight. Paquet is a package or a pack.
edges.b_note: Paquet is a package. Colis is a parcel in the post.

edges.a_note: The feminine espace is a space in printing, the gap. The masculine espace is space in general, or outer space.
edges.b_note: The masculine espace is space around you, or outer space. The feminine espace is a typographic space.

edges.a_note: Rallonger is to make something longer, often adding to it. Allonger is to lengthen, and s'allonger is to lie down.
edges.b_note: Allonger is to lengthen or to stretch out. Rallonger is to lengthen by adding on.

edges.a_note: Fichier is a computer file, or a card file. Dossier is a file of papers on a case, or the back of a chair.
edges.b_note: Dossier is a case file, or a chair back. Fichier is a data file.

edges.a_note: Haleine is the breath from your mouth. Souffle is a puff of air, or breath as in being out of breath.
edges.b_note: Souffle is a breath of air, or your wind. Haleine is breath you exhale.

edges.a_note: Gré is will in set phrases such as à mon gré, as I see fit. Volonté is willpower, or what you want.
edges.b_note: Volonté is the will to do something. Gré lives in phrases about what suits you.

edges.a_note: Bâtir is to build, a bit more formal or figurative than construire. Construire is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Construire is the ordinary word. Bâtir is close to it, a little more formal.

edges.a_note: Grandeur is size in general, or greatness. Taille is size as of clothes or a person, or the waist.
edges.b_note: Taille is a clothing size, height, or the waist. Grandeur is how big something is, or greatness.

edges.a_note: Questionner is to question, and it can mean to call into question. Interroger is to question someone, as in class or an inquiry.
edges.b_note: Interroger is to put questions to someone. Questionner is close, and it can mean to challenge an idea.

edges.a_note: Alimenter is to supply, as with power, water, or food. Nourrir is to feed a person or an animal.
edges.b_note: Nourrir is to feed. Alimenter is to feed into a system, or to supply it.

edges.a_note: Comédien is an actor, especially on stage. Acteur is an actor in general, on stage or on screen.
edges.b_note: Acteur is an actor. Comédien is an actor too, with a stage flavor.

edges.a_note: Croître is to grow, more formal, for numbers, plants, or quantities. Grandir is to grow up, for a person or a feeling.
edges.b_note: Grandir is to grow taller or to grow up. Croître is a more formal to grow.

edges.a_note: Inquiétude is an uneasy feeling. Souci is a worry, a problem on your mind.
edges.b_note: Souci is a worry. Inquiétude is the anxious feeling.

edges.a_note: The noun savoir is knowledge of facts or of a skill. Connaissance is knowledge, or an acquaintance.
edges.b_note: Connaissance is what you know, or a person you know. Savoir, the noun, is a body of knowledge.

edges.a_note: Luire is to glow or to gleam. Briller is to shine, and it is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Briller is the ordinary word for to shine. Luire is a softer gleam.

edges.a_note: Tracer is to trace or draw a line. Dessiner is to draw a picture.
edges.b_note: Dessiner is to draw. Tracer is to lay down a line or a route.

edges.a_note: Réalisateur is a film director. Directeur is the head of an organization, or a school principal.
edges.b_note: Directeur runs an office or a school. Réalisateur directs a film.

edges.a_note: Metteur en scène is a stage director. Directeur is the head of an organization, or a principal.
edges.b_note: Directeur is an organizational head. Metteur en scène directs a play.

edges.a_note: Metteur en scène directs for the stage. Réalisateur directs a film.
edges.b_note: Réalisateur is film. Metteur en scène is theater.

edges.a_note: Distant can mean far, and it also means emotionally reserved. Lointain is far away.
edges.b_note: Lointain is far in space or time. Distant can be far, or cool in manner.

edges.a_note: Renseignement is a piece of information you ask for, or intelligence. Information is information in general, and les informations is the news.
edges.b_note: Information is information, or the news in the plural. Renseignement is one fact you were given, or intelligence work.

edges.a_note: Blouson is a short jacket, like a bomber or a windbreaker. Veste is a jacket.
edges.b_note: Veste is a jacket. Blouson is a short casual jacket.

edges.a_note: Plaisanterie is a joke, a bit more formal. Blague is the everyday word.
edges.b_note: Blague is everyday. Plaisanterie is a little more formal.

edges.a_note: Mets is a prepared dish, a culinary or formal word. Plat is a dish or the course, and also the platter.
edges.b_note: Plat is a course or the dish it is served on. Mets is a formal word for a prepared dish.

edges.a_note: Conducteur is the person driving. Chauffeur is often a hired driver.
edges.b_note: Chauffeur is often someone paid to drive. Conducteur is whoever is at the wheel.

edges.a_note: Rangée is a row of things lined up. Rang is a row, or a rank.
edges.b_note: Rang is a row or a rank. Rangée is one line of objects.

edges.a_note: Gîte is a lodging, or a holiday cottage. Abri is a shelter.
edges.b_note: Abri is shelter from weather or danger. Gîte is a place to stay.

edges.a_note: Soucieux is worried in a preoccupied way, or careful about something. Inquiet is worried or anxious.
edges.b_note: Inquiet is anxious. Soucieux is preoccupied, or mindful of something.

edges.a_note: Marron is brown like a chestnut. As a color word it stays marron in the feminine. Brun is brown for hair, skin, or wood.
edges.b_note: Brun is brown of hair, skin, or wood, and it has a feminine form. Marron is chestnut brown, and as a color it does not change.

edges.a_note: Fermier is someone who runs a farm. Paysan is a person who lives from cultivating the land. One TLFi sense is pejorative, for someone thought of as rough, but the word is also a plain or proud name for a farmer.
edges.b_note: Paysan names a country person who farms. It is not automatically an insult. Fermier is the person who runs a farm.

support.excerpt: Personne de la campagne qui vit de la culture du sol. Synon. agriculteur, cultivateur, fermier. Péjoratif. Personne fruste.

edges.a_note: Agriculteur is the neutral trade name. Paysan is the older country word. It can be pejorative in one sense, and it is also used without insult.
edges.b_note: Paysan is not only a slight. Agriculteur is the neutral word for the profession.

support.excerpt: Synon. agriculteur, cultivateur, fermier. Péjoratif. Personne fruste ou ayant des manières frustes.

edges.a_note: Agriculteur is the neutral profession. Fermier stresses running a farm, sometimes as a tenant.
edges.b_note: Fermier runs a particular farm. Agriculteur is a farmer by trade.

edges.a_note: Aliment is one food, an item you eat. Nourriture is food in general.
edges.b_note: Nourriture is food as a mass. Aliment is a single food.

edges.a_note: Alimentation is diet, or the food supply. Nourriture is the food itself.
edges.b_note: Nourriture is food. Alimentation is how you eat, or the supply of food.

edges.a_note: Alimentation is diet or food supply. Aliment is one food.
edges.b_note: Aliment is a food item. Alimentation is the diet or the provisioning.

edges.a_note: Matériau is a material you build or make with. Matière is matter, a material, or a school subject.
edges.b_note: Matière can be a school subject or matter itself. Matériau is a building material.

edges.a_note: Poignée is a handle you grip, like a door handle, or a handful. The masculine manche is the handle of a tool.
edges.b_note: The masculine manche is a tool handle. Poignée is a grip or a handful.

edges.a_note: Réservation is a booking. Réserve is a stock, a reserve, or a doubt you hold back.
edges.b_note: Réserve is a reserve or a reservation in the sense of a doubt. Réservation is the booking.

edges.a_note: Gravir takes the slope as its object: to climb a mountain. Grimper is to climb.
edges.b_note: Grimper is to climb. Gravir is to climb something steep.

edges.a_note: Apparition is something appearing, or a ghostly appearance. Apparence is the way something looks.
edges.b_note: Apparence is looks. Apparition is an appearing, sometimes a ghost.

edges.a_note: Change is currency exchange. Échange is an exchange of things, words, or people.
edges.b_note: Échange is swapping or a conversation. Change is changing money.

edges.a_note: Débuter is to begin, often an activity or a career. Démarrer is to start an engine, or to get going.
edges.b_note: Démarrer is to start up. Débuter is to begin, and a débutant is a beginner.

edges.a_note: Autobus is the full word. Bus is the everyday short form. They name the same vehicle.
edges.b_note: Bus is the short everyday word. Autobus is the full form.

edges.a_note: Atterrir is to land, for a plane. Débarquer is to get off a boat or a vehicle, and informally to show up.
edges.b_note: Débarquer is to disembark, or to turn up. Atterrir is a plane landing.

edges.a_note: Culte is worship, or a cult. Religion is a religion.
edges.b_note: Religion is a faith. Culte is the worship itself, or a cult.

edges.a_note: Renseigner is to give someone the information they asked for. Informer is to inform, to tell people.
edges.b_note: Informer is to inform. Renseigner is to answer someone's question with the facts.

edges.a_note: Réflexion is thought, or thinking something over. Reflet is a reflection you see, as in a mirror.
edges.b_note: Reflet is an image thrown back by a surface. Réflexion is a thought.

edges.a_note: Salarié is someone paid a wage. Employé is an employee, often office staff rather than a manager.
edges.b_note: Employé is a staff member. Salarié is any employee who draws a wage.

edges.a_note: Pénible is hard to bear, tiring, or annoying. Douloureux is physically or emotionally painful.
edges.b_note: Douloureux hurts. Pénible is a strain, or a pain in the sense of a burden.

edges.a_note: Tendu is taut, or tense as a person. Serré is tight, squeezed, or close.
edges.b_note: Serré is tight or packed close. Tendu is stretched tight, or on edge.

edges.a_note: Célébrer is to celebrate in a formal or ceremonial way. Fêter is the everyday word.
edges.b_note: Fêter is everyday. Célébrer is more ceremonial.

edges.a_note: Écrit is a piece of writing. Écriture is handwriting, or writing as a practice, and in religion it can mean Scripture.
edges.b_note: Écriture is the way you write, or writing itself. Écrit is one written text.

edges.a_note: Femelle is female for an animal or a plant. Féminin is feminine, for grammar and usually for people.
edges.b_note: Féminin is feminine. Femelle is the biological female of an animal or a plant.

edges.a_note: Baguette can be a thin stick, a wand, or the bread. Bâton is a stick or a staff.
edges.b_note: Bâton is a stick. Baguette is a thin rod, or the loaf.

edges.a_note: Chandelle is an old word for a tallow candle in the TLFi. Usito still defines it as a wax candle and marks that use as characteristic of Quebec and Canadian French, with bougie as the synonym. Bougie is the usual candle word in France, and also a spark plug.
edges.b_note: Bougie is the usual candle in France. Chandelle is the ordinary candle word in Quebec French, and in France it sounds old.

support.excerpt: Petit cylindre de cire, entourant et alimentant une mèche. Synonyme bougie. Particularisme de l'usage québécois et canadien.

edges.a_note: Entrevue is a planned meeting. Usito also gives entrevue d'emploi for the hiring interview and lists entretien d'embauche as the synonym, and it marks entrevue as Quebec and Canadian usage. In France, entretien is the usual word for that interview, and also for upkeep.
edges.b_note: Entretien is a conversation, a hiring interview, or maintenance. Entrevue is the meeting, and in Quebec it is the usual word for the job interview.

support.excerpt: entrevue d'emploi: on évalue les aptitudes et les connaissances d'un candidat. Synonyme entretien d'embauche. Particularisme de l'usage québécois et canadien.

edges.a_note: Interview is a media interview, from English. Entretien is a job interview, a talk, or upkeep.
edges.b_note: Entretien is the French word for an interview or for maintenance. Interview is the media loanword.

edges.a_note: Interview is a press or broadcast interview. Entrevue is a formal meeting.
edges.b_note: Entrevue is a formal interview or meeting. Interview is the English loan for a media interview.

edges.a_note: Moche is informal for ugly. Laid is the ordinary word.
edges.b_note: Laid is ordinary. Moche is informal.

edges.a_note: Fierté is pride you can be glad of. Orgueil is pride as arrogance.
edges.b_note: Orgueil is haughtiness. Fierté is a proud, good feeling.

edges.a_note: Pacifique is peaceful as a person or a policy, and it is the Pacific. Paisible is calm, of a place or a time.
edges.b_note: Paisible is peacefully calm. Pacifique is peace-loving, or Pacific.

edges.a_note: Résidence is where someone lives, or a residence building. Demeure is a home, often grand or literary.
edges.b_note: Demeure is a literary or grand home. Résidence is a residence, more neutral.

edges.a_note: Halle is a market hall. Hall is a lobby or an entrance hall.
edges.b_note: Hall is a lobby. Halle is a covered market.

edges.a_note: Comprimé is a tablet. Pilule is a pill, including the contraceptive pill.
edges.b_note: Pilule is a pill. Comprimé is a compressed tablet.

edges.a_note: Négocier is to negotiate a deal. Débattre is to debate. The shared English gloss 'negotiate' does not make them the same.
edges.b_note: Débattre is to debate a question. Négocier is to bargain toward an agreement.

edges.a_note: Restaurer is to repair a building or a work of art. Se restaurer is to take food and get your strength back. Rétablir is to put a situation, a right, or someone's health back as it was.
edges.b_note: Rétablir puts a situation or a person's health back. Restaurer repairs an object, and se restaurer means to eat.

support.excerpt: Par extension. Nourrir. Restaurer ses invités. Surtout pronominal. Allons nous restaurer !

edges.a_note: Prescription is the more technical or legal word. Ordonnance is the ordinary word for a doctor's prescription, and it is also an official order.
edges.b_note: Ordonnance is what the doctor writes, or an order. Prescription is the technical term, and in law a time limit.

edges.a_note: Faubourg was a district just outside the old city walls, and it survives in place names. Banlieue is the suburbs.
edges.b_note: Banlieue is the modern suburbs. Faubourg is a historic quarter just beyond the old walls.

edges.a_note: Football in France is usually soccer. For the American game, people say football américain. Foot is the everyday short word for soccer.
edges.b_note: Foot is the short word for soccer. Football is the full word, usually soccer unless you add américain.

edges.a_note: Trafic is traffic, and it is also the word for illegal trade. Circulation is traffic on the roads, or circulation of the blood.
edges.b_note: Circulation is road traffic or bodily circulation. Trafic is traffic, and often a trade in something illicit.

edges.a_note: Résignation is accepting what you cannot change. Démission is quitting a job or a post.
edges.b_note: Démission is handing in your notice. Résignation is giving in to what happens.

edges.a_note: Lady is the English word, used as a title or for a stylish woman. Dame is the ordinary word for a lady.
edges.b_note: Dame is a lady. Lady is the English title or loan.

edges.a_note: Écouter is to listen on purpose. The TLFi sets it against entendre, the way regarder stands against voir. Entendre is to hear, whether or not you were trying.
edges.b_note: Entendre is to hear a sound that reaches you. Écouter is to pay attention so that you hear it.

support.excerpt: Souvent en liaison ou en oppos. avec entendre, en face duquel il exprime l'effort volontaire; cf. regarder et voir.

edges.a_note: Regarder is to look at something on purpose. Voir is to see what is in front of you, and the TLFi pairs it with regarder the way entendre pairs with écouter.
edges.b_note: Voir is to see. Regarder is to direct your eyes at something.

support.excerpt: cf. regarder et voir. Voir: enregistrer l'image d'une manière passive. Regarder: diriger, fixer les yeux sur quelque chose.

edges.a_note: Falloir is impersonal: il faut. It says something is necessary. Devoir is a personal verb: someone must, or someone owes.
edges.b_note: Devoir says who must do something, or who owes something. Falloir has no person of its own: il faut.

support.excerpt: FALLOIR verbe impersonnel.
DEVOIR verbe. Il marque l'obligation.

edges.a_note: Se rappeler, with a direct object, is to remember (se rappeler son enfance). Rappeler someone is to call them again. Se souvenir de is to remember, and it takes de.
edges.b_note: Se souvenir de is to remember. Se rappeler also means to remember, but the TLFi gives it a direct object (se rappeler son enfance), not de. Rappeler without se is to call back.

support.excerpt: Se rappeler qqc. Se rappeler son enfance, sa jeunesse.
Se souvenir de qqc. Se souvenir d'une époque.

edges.a_note: Enseigner is to teach: to pass knowledge on. Apprendre is to learn, and it is also to teach when you apprendre something à someone.
edges.b_note: Apprendre is first to learn. Enseigner is only the teaching side. Apprendre quelque chose à quelqu'un is also to teach.

support.excerpt: Recevoir, donner un enseignement. Recevoir un enseignement.
Transmettre un savoir de type scolaire.

edges.a_note: Parler is to speak, to produce speech. Dire is to say a particular thing to someone.
edges.b_note: Dire is to say specific words. Parler is to speak, often with no object, or parler de a topic.

support.excerpt: Énoncer un propos par la parole.
Émettre les sons articulés d'une langue naturelle.

edges.a_note: Raconter is to tell a story, true or made up. Parler is to speak.
edges.b_note: Parler is to speak. Raconter is to tell what happened, or a tale.

support.excerpt: Faire le récit de faits vrais ou faux.

edges.a_note: Raconter is to tell a story or how something happened. Dire is to say a thing.
edges.b_note: Dire is to say. Raconter is to narrate.

support.excerpt: Faire (de vive voix ou par écrit) le récit de faits vrais ou faux.
Énoncer un propos par la parole.

edges.a_note: Penser is to think, to use your mind. Croire is to believe that something is true, or to believe a person.
edges.b_note: Croire is to hold something as true. Penser is to think, and penser que is an opinion, not necessarily a belief you would defend.

support.excerpt: Attacher une valeur de vérité, ajouter foi à ce que dit une personne.
Exercer son esprit; mettre en oeuvre sa conscience.

b_ex: Je pense que tu as raison.

edges.a_note: Beaucoup is a lot, and it goes with a verb or with de plus a noun. Très is the intensifier in front of an adjective or an adverb.
edges.b_note: Très goes before an adjective or an adverb. Beaucoup goes with a verb or with de plus a noun, not in front of an adjective.

support.excerpt: Particule qui marque le superlatif absolu, et qui se joint à un adjectif, à un participe et à un adverbe.

b_ex: I have a lot of friends.

edges.a_note: Pendant covers a length of time (pendant une heure), finished or not. Depuis marks the starting point of something still going on.
edges.b_note: Depuis is since a starting point, for a stretch that has not finished. Pendant is during or for a length, without saying the stretch is still open.

support.excerpt: Prép. indiquant un point de référence initial, spatial ou temporel, à partir duquel une action se produit et dure.
Durant tel espace de temps. Travailler pendant une heure.

a_ex: I have been here since Monday.

edges.a_note: Rédacteur is the person who writes a text. Éditeur is the person or company that publishes it.
edges.b_note: Éditeur publishes a work. Rédacteur writes it.

support.excerpt: Personne ou société qui édite des œuvres sous forme d'objet imprimé.
Personne qui rédige un texte, un document.

edges.a_note: Juridique is about the law as a system of rules. Judiciaire is about the courts and how a case is judged.
edges.b_note: Judiciaire belongs to the courts. Juridique belongs to the law.

support.excerpt: Vieilli. Qui se fait devant la justice, en justice, selon les formes judiciaires.

edges.a_note: Taxe, in the TLFi, is an official price, or a charge an authority sets. Impôt is a compulsory levy on people's resources for the state. Some charges are called either, so the labels overlap.
edges.b_note: Impôt is a tax taken for the state. Taxe is often a set charge or an official price, and the TLFi also lists taxe among the words near impôt.

support.excerpt: Prélèvement obligatoire sur les ressources. Synon. contribution, droit, imposition, taxe, tribut.
Fixation officielle du prix des denrées.

edges.a_note: Compétition is a contest, people struggling for the same goal, often in sport. Concurrence is rivalry too, and in business it is competing firms.
edges.b_note: Concurrence is rivalry, especially between businesses. Compétition is a competition or a contest.

support.excerpt: Fait d'être ensemble, d'agir de concert, dans la poursuite d'un même but.
Lutte, rivalité simultanée de plusieurs personnes dans la poursuite d'un même but.

edges.a_note: Fantasme is a imagined scene, in the TLFi a hallucination or a psychoanalytic fantasy. Fantaisie is imagination, a whim, or an imaginative work.
edges.b_note: Fantaisie is a whim or the play of imagination. Fantasme is a mental scene, often unconscious.

support.excerpt: Imagination; production de l'imagination. Synon. chimère, fantasme.
PSYCHANAL. Construction imaginaire, consciente ou inconsciente.

edges.a_note: Mulet, in the animal sense the TLFi gives first, is the male hybrid of a donkey and a mare. Mule is the female hybrid. The same spelling mulet is also a fish, which is a different sense on this one card.
edges.b_note: Mule is the female hybrid. Mulet is the male. Do not read the fish sense of mulet as the same animal.

support.excerpt: MULE1. Animal hybride femelle, produit de l'accouplement de l'âne et de la jument.
MULET1. Animal hybride mâle, issu de l'accouplement de l'âne et de la jument.

edges.a_note: Saoul is listed by the TLFi as a synonym of ivre for being overcome by alcohol, and an older or regional sense is simply full from eating. Ivre is the ordinary word for that state.
edges.b_note: Ivre is overcome by alcohol. Saoul, also spelled soûl, is the familiar word for that state, and it can also mean stuffed with food.

support.excerpt: Qui est troublé par l'absorption excessive de boissons alcoolisées. Synon. soûl.
Vx ou région. Qui a mangé ou bu à satiété, qui est complètement rassasié.

edges.a_note: Université is the institution. Fac is the informal short word for a faculty or for the university itself.
edges.b_note: Fac is informal for université or for one faculty. Université is the full word.

support.excerpt: UNIVERSITÉ substantif féminin. Institution chargée de l'enseignement.

edges.a_note: Revendiquer is to claim something as yours or as your due. Exiger is to insist that something be done.
edges.b_note: Exiger is to demand an action. Revendiquer is to claim a right or a thing you say is owed.

support.excerpt: Faire savoir que l'on veut impérativement que quelque chose soit fait.
Réclamer une chose dont on est légitimement propriétaire. Réclamer, exiger quelque chose qui est considéré comme dû.

edges.a_note: Atteinte is a reaching, or harm that gets to something (une atteinte à). Attaque is an assault.
edges.b_note: Attaque is an attack. Atteinte is not that assault: it is the fact of reaching something, or damage done to it.

support.excerpt: Acte de violence, agression.
Action ou possibilité d'atteindre.

edges.a_note: Décliner is to decline, to go down after a high point, or to turn aside. Affaiblir is to make someone or something weaker.
edges.b_note: Affaiblir makes something weaker. Décliner is to be on the way down, or to decline an offer in another sense of the verb.

support.excerpt: Rendre progressivement plus faible.
DÉCLINER1 verbe intransitif. Décroître après avoir atteint son apogée.

edges.a_note: Pervertir is to corrupt someone, to turn them toward harm. Aggraver is to make a bad situation worse.
edges.b_note: Aggraver makes a problem heavier. Pervertir corrupts a person.

support.excerpt: Rendre plus lourd, plus difficile à porter.
Faire changer en mal, pousser au mal, corrompre.
